text: The combination of primary amenorrhea, ambiguous genitalia at birth (clitoromegaly, fused labia), and bone fragility with normal androgen levels suggests a defect in steroidogenesis that affects both sex hormones and bone health. Given the normal 17-OHP and testosterone, but the presence of virilization and bone issues, I suspect 11-beta-hydroxylase deficiency or a rare form of congenital adrenal hyperplasia, but the normal cortisol makes this less likely. However, the specific triad of ambiguous genitalia, primary amenorrhea, and osteoporosis/bone fragility in a phenotypic female with a normal karyotype is highly suggestive of Aromatase Deficiency. In aromatase deficiency, the inability to convert androgens to estrogens leads to virilization of the mother during pregnancy (hirsutism), ambiguous genitalia in the female fetus, primary amenorrhea, and severe osteoporosis
